title: Implement layout-aware store, kernel, and recovery
description:
Give the JSON and in-memory backends the final recovered mutation session: one capture/apply storage capability over the canonical layout, staged publication of an absent data root, the exact delta/journal action set including `DeleteFile`, and identity-safe rollback and recovery. This package builds on the pure declaration, image, capture, and managed-document primitives already present on the integration branch and adds the storage and transaction boundary beneath them.

## Background

Repository mutations must publish all coupled persisted state through one recoverable transaction so a failure leaves either the complete old repository state or the complete new state. Today publication is split across per-file and command-semantic storage methods with independent recovery routes. This package introduces a single storage session that captures a `RepositoryImage` and applies one finalized `RepositoryDelta`, with recovery running before any read.

## What to build

- Final storage capability and kernel: `RepositoryStateStore::open_mutation_session(layout)` is the only entry to affected storage mutation — no per-file or command-semantic method survives. The recovered opaque session captures a `RepositoryImage` and applies one finalized `RepositoryDelta`. `JsonFileStorage` implements it with root-confined capabilities for both layout roots and a `FileTransactionKernel` constructed from the explicit layout/capability set. `InMemoryStorage` locks one aggregate state, models both virtual roots plus recovery residue/failures, and clones/apply-validates/swaps on success under the same session contract. Both backends run one shared conformance suite proving identical images, preconditions, action ordering, failure points, result hashes, and rollback/no-swap outcomes.
- Mandatory recovered-session boundary: `open_mutation_session(layout)` acquires repository-root bootstrap serialization, recovers external journals/residue, and — when the selected root exists — acquires data-root repository and event guards, recovers internal journals/residue, and only then permits capture. Guard order is bootstrap → repository → events (claim flows enter already holding coordinator, yielding coordinator → bootstrap → repository → events); later-guard holders cannot enter coordination. Recovery/residue/root-alias failure prevents capture. Retained CLI sessions are reentrant only for the same canonical layout.
- Exact delta and journal vocabulary: actions are `CreateDirectory`, `WriteFile`, `SetMode`, and `DeleteFile`; each carries a canonical `VirtualPath`, producer/ownership identity, normalized expected preimage (absent / file hash+size+mode / directory+mode / symlink payload+mode / unsupported kind), and final identity. Normalization rejects duplicate canonical paths and any cross-root pair resolving to one physical identity. Each durable journal action stores canonical root class plus normalized relative path — never an absolute or `.jit`-prefixed surrogate — and recovery resolves it through the journal-bound layout identity, rejecting layout mismatch/alias and rechecking physical uniqueness. Immediately before journal preparation, revalidate the entire read set and root identity while the session is held, returning a typed retryable conflict on any content/listing/root/alias change.
- Recoverable `DeleteFile`: extend `TransactionAction`, `JournalActionKind`, plan normalization, hashing, preparation, publication, rollback, and recovery. Preparation verifies the normalized expected regular-file identity, creates and synchronizes the rollback backup, and durably records original and final-absent identities before publication. Publication rechecks the preimage, removes the target without following links, synchronizes the parent, and marks progress. Rollback restores the verified backup with no-replace safety. Prepared-journal recovery converges to the original file; committed-journal recovery verifies absence and completes cleanup. Delete never targets a directory.
- Absent-data-root publication: for an absent selected data root, assemble the complete root in a verified sibling staging directory reached through no-follow capabilities (symlink/unsupported ancestry rejected); all `Data(...)` actions target the staging capability while the durable journal remains `Worktree(Descendant(".jit-bootstrap/transactions/..."))`. After all staged content/modes are verified and synchronized, the kernel atomically publishes the staged directory with a no-replace rename, fsyncs the parent, opens the final root no-follow, and verifies its object identity. The successful rename is the irreversible commit point: recovery never removes or replaces a published root. A lost no-replace rename fails with a typed occupied-destination error leaving no partial state; a subsequent invocation opens the existing root through the ordinary path. Mixed deltas order every semantic `Worktree(...)` action after the data-root rename. Once the root exists, internal journals live at `Data(Descendant("tmp/transactions/..."))`.
- Recoverable terminology: documentation and results say "recoverable transaction" and "converges to a complete old/new state" — never filesystem-wide instantaneous atomicity.

Distilled §2 contracts: final storage capability and kernel, mandatory recovered-session boundary, exact delta and journal vocabulary, recoverable `DeleteFile`, absent-data-root publication, and recoverable terminology. See `dev/active/cdc840ad-plan.md` §2 and plan decisions D4, D5, D6, D11, D20 for full detail. This preserves `@/inv/atomic-writes` (verified staging plus atomic no-replace publication so an occupied destination is never overwritten).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Default/nested/disjoint/overlap/alias and existing/absent-root conformance passes on both backends.
- [hard] REQ-02: Every publication/recovery failure point, concurrent-creation race, and occupied-destination outcome passes targeted plus prior cumulative tests with no partial root visibility.

## Constraints

- Cumulative, final-form commits on branch `integration/cdc840ad`; never merged to main individually. Each commit runs targeted tests plus all prior cumulative package tests on both backends.
- No adapter, feature flag, compatibility re-export, dual path, temporary API, or wrapper forwarding old publishers. Expose only the final interfaces the next package requires.
- Only two physical journal locations exist: external `Worktree(.jit-bootstrap/transactions)` before the data root exists and internal `Data(tmp/transactions)` after; no other physical `.jit` literal is permitted.
- Out of scope (plan D19/D20): lease credential/claim-log/claim-command redesign; and any worktree/data-root binding redesign that would adopt a disjoint root as a repository mid-operation.

Blast radius: storage traits/backends, locks and capabilities, transaction plan/journal/kernel/recovery, and init/profile storage tests.
